technical.lead: Azure clears $100 billion; Meta's free cash flow falls to $784 million
technical.body: Microsoft and Meta both reported after the close on Wednesday, July 29, and the tape sorted them in opposite directions on Thursday, July 30. The two prints are not like-for-like beyond sharing a reporting evening: Microsoft's are fiscal fourth-quarter figures that close its fiscal year, Meta's are calendar second-quarter figures. Microsoft posted revenue of $90.0 billion, up 18%, operating income of $40.6 billion, also up 18%, net income of $35.8 billion and diluted earnings per share of $4.81 as reported and $4.74 excluding a one-off, against a Street estimate nearer $4.24. The line that moved the price was Azure and other cloud services revenue up 43%, with the press release recording that Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time in a fiscal year. Microsoft Cloud revenue was $59.3 billion, up 27%, the Intelligent Cloud segment $39.3 billion, up 32%, Microsoft 365 Copilot passed 30 million paid seats and GitHub Copilot 50 million users. Capital expenditure including finance leases was $41 billion in the quarter, of which $5.6 billion was finance leases and roughly two thirds went to short-lived assets — the processors and accelerators absorbing customer demand — and Microsoft brought up 31 datacentres across five continents in the quarter, 88 across the fiscal year. Chief financial officer Amy Hood guided first-quarter capital spend above $50 billion and first-quarter Azure growth of approximately 45% in constant currency, said demand continues to exceed available supply, and disclosed an accounting change effective fiscal 2027: the estimated useful life of datacentres and office buildings extends from 15 to 25 years, which pushes leases from finance to operating treatment and, because capital expenditure counts finance leases but not operating ones, lowers the calendar-2026 capital expenditure expectation to roughly $175 billion while leaving the underlying investment unchanged. Meta's June quarter ran the other way. Revenue was $60.801 billion, up 28% and ahead of consensus, but total costs and expenses rose 55% to $42.026 billion — carrying $2.40 billion of charges related to legal proceedings and $1.18 billion of severance from the May 2026 workforce reduction — so income from operations fell 8% to $18.775 billion, the operating margin compressed to 31% from 43% a year earlier, net income fell 14% to $15.848 billion and diluted earnings per share fell 13% to $6.18. Capital expenditure of $31.08 billion in the quarter cut free cash flow to $784 million. Meta narrowed its full-year 2026 capital expenditure outlook from $125-145 billion to $130-145 billion — a lift at the floor rather than a cut at the ceiling — guided third-quarter revenue to $61-64 billion, a midpoint under the Street, and reported headcount of 75,472, down 1% from a year earlier. TS2's July 30 market report has Microsoft up 15.2% and Meta down 8.9% on the session, with the semiconductor complex riding Microsoft's coat-tails: Lam Research up 20.9%, Micron up 15.45%, AMD up 7.3% and Arm up 7.1%, against Qualcomm down 2.8%. The Motley Fool's midday snapshot at 12:13 PM ET had Microsoft up 15.5%. Second-quarter gross domestic product growth came in at 1.5%, below forecast, and core personal consumption expenditure inflation at 3.3%, softer than expected, with the Federal Reserve holding rates.

technical.lead: Samsung books a record quarter on server memory; the handset unit posts a loss
technical.body: Samsung Electronics announced second-quarter results on Thursday, July 30: consolidated revenue of KRW 171.5 trillion, up 28% from the first quarter and an all-time high, operating profit of KRW 89.5 trillion, also an all-time high, and earnings per share of KRW 10,849, up 52%. The Device Solutions division is the whole of it — revenue of KRW 127.5 trillion and operating profit of KRW 89.2 trillion on sales up 56% quarter on quarter. The Memory Business credits prioritising server products under limited capacity, which took its share of server revenue to a record high; it scaled up HBM4 sales and shipped what it describes as the industry's first HBM4E samples to major customers. The contrast inside the same company is the part worth holding onto: the Mobile eXperience and Networks businesses posted an operating loss of KRW 0.7 trillion, with revenue up year on year on Galaxy S26 and Galaxy A sales but earnings down on elevated component cost pressure across the industry — the memory cycle paying Samsung's Device Solutions division is the same cycle charging Samsung's handset unit. For the second half Samsung expects robust server-led demand from continued AI infrastructure capital expenditure and broader adoption of agentic AI, with growth in server DRAM, enterprise solid-state drives and HBM accelerating and the market staying undersupplied even as mobile and PC demand partially moderates. TradingKey puts the operating profit at KRW 89.49 trillion, roughly $62 billion, up 1,813.8% against the same quarter of 2025, makes this the third quarter running in which Samsung has set an operating-profit record, and relays management guidance that judging on 2027 orders already received the supply-demand gap widens further than in 2026.

technical.lead: A CVSS 10.0 flaw left 233 privileged tools open on Ruflo's MCP bridge
technical.body: Noma Labs disclosed CVE-2026-59726, which it named RufRoot, on Wednesday, July 29, with the trade write-ups following on Thursday, July 30; it carries the maximum CVSS score of 10.0. The affected project is Ruflo, an open-source multi-agent orchestration platform that began life as Claude Flow and now serves as a harness for Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's Codex, with more than 66,500 GitHub stars. The defect sits in its Model Context Protocol bridge, an Express.js server that brokers every tool invocation across agent workflows. That bridge's POST /mcp endpoint had no authentication, and the shipped docker-compose configuration bound port 3001 to 0.0.0.0, so a default self-hosted deployment published 233 high-privilege tools — shell command execution, database operations, agent management and memory storage — to anyone who could reach the port. A single unauthenticated HTTP request invoking the terminal-execution tool runs commands inside the container as the node user; from there an attacker can read stored user conversations, lift the environment variables holding model API keys, reach a MongoDB instance that was running without authentication, spawn agent swarms billed to the victim's own keys, write persistent payloads into the /app directory, and poison the AgentDB learning store so that the outputs served to every other user of that deployment are tainted. Noma's framing is that the bridge is not an auxiliary debug interface but the platform's central nervous system, controlling all tool calls and agent actions. Every release before 3.16.3 is affected; maintainer Reuven Cohen shipped 3.16.3 within 24 hours of the June 30 responsible disclosure, binding the bridge to loopback, requiring a bearer token, gating terminal execution behind explicit opt-in, enabling MongoDB authentication and tightening container and cross-origin controls. The half of the problem that does not patch away is the memory poisoning: Amit Jena, an AI development manager at Kanerika quoted in CSO Online's coverage, argues that adoption of the protocol has outrun the security defaults built into orchestration tooling, and that poisoned agent memory is not a product-specific failure.

technical.lead: Unit 42 reconstructs a DeepSeek campaign the agent ran end to end while every exploit it tried failed
technical.body: Unit 42 published on Thursday, July 30 a reconstruction of a campaign in which an operator tracked as knaithe, also seen as KnYuan and based in Zhuhai, wired DeepSeek into the Hermes Agent framework and drove it from Telegram as an autonomous offensive operator. The observed autonomous phase ran in early May 2026. The agent enumerated vulnerabilities across ten product families, pulled proof-of-concept code from GitHub, ran FOFA queries to find live targets, checked their versions and form endpoints, and then attempted exploitation itself. Seven vulnerabilities were in scope, and the split between what the machine did and what the human did is the finding. On its own the agent tried Langflow's CVE-2026-33017 at CVSS 9.8, which needed auto-login enabled or a public flow identifier, and the n8n pair CVE-2026-21858 and CVE-2025-68613 at 10.0 and 9.9, which needed an unauthenticated upload form and met authentication instead — and failed on all three. The confirmed compromises were manual: data exfiltration from three organisations through Citrix NetScaler's CVE-2026-3055 at 9.8, and command execution on Marimo Notebook instances through CVE-2026-39987 at 9.8. Reverse-shell attempts against Apache Tomcat's CVE-2026-34486 and a Windows IKE VPN flaw, CVE-2026-33824 at 9.8, went nowhere, and a PAN-OS proof of concept for CVE-2026-0300 was cloned but never worked. The target arithmetic is worth keeping: FOFA showed 647,017 n8n instances worldwide and 25,209 inside China, the agent sampled roughly 100 of the Chinese ones and probed about 40 unique addresses, and across more than 460 targeted systems Unit 42 counts three confirmed exploitations. Model selection was deliberate and it is the part with the longest shelf life. The operator used Claude Code for connectivity and proxy validation and Codex traces in the exploit-development directories, evaluated Qwen, GLM, Kimi and MiniMax, and ran the campaign itself on DeepSeek; OpenAI's safety systems refused the requests that violated its policies and disabled an account linked to the activity.

technical.lead: Unsloth merges the fix for a bug that disabled reasoning on larger Qwen models
technical.body: With v0.1.51-beta tagged on Wednesday afternoon, July 29, and the 2026.7.6 wheel published, Unsloth added no new release tag on Thursday, July 30 and instead merged a run of fixes straight into main. Pull request 7289 is the substantive one. Multi-turn conversations with Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6 were losing reasoning content between turns because the ChatMessage model had no reasoning_content field, so Pydantic dropped it silently before the request ever reached the inference server; the same change fixes a size-detection bug that read Qwen3.5-35B-A3B as a 3-billion-parameter model by preferring the active-expert count over the total, which switched reasoning off by default on the larger models outright. The fix adds the field, replaces the size extraction with an anchored pattern that scans path segments from the right and accepts both B and M suffixes, teaches the overflow retry path to clip reasoning content when the context runs over, emits an empty content string on reasoning-only assistant turns for llama.cpp compatibility, and mirrors the pattern into the TypeScript frontend so client-side gating agrees with the backend; 12,583 backend tests pass against a single pre-existing failure, 32 pass on the frontend, and 368 model identifier variants were exercised. Pull request 7631 closes a genuinely dangerous default: uninstall.sh and uninstall.ps1 ignored their arguments entirely, so a --help flag or a mistyped option uninstalled the product, and the shell script could partially remove an installation if a curl-to-shell stream was truncated mid-download. The uninstallers now print usage and remove nothing on a help flag, reject an unrecognised argument before any destructive step, and wrap the removal body in a function invoked from a compound block so a truncated download parses to nothing, verified across 25 shell and 39 PowerShell argument tests. Pull request 7645 routes six explicit Vulkan setup failures in the Studio setup scripts through the failure helpers rather than bare exits, so a user who asked for Vulkan and hit a failure now sees the error in Studio desktop instead of a silent stop, with 26 shell installer test files clean and 1,387 Python tests passing.
